messages:
maya: quick heads-up: ran into a hang in the Go generator sample when an auth token rotated mid-stream. iter.Next() sometimes never returns even after ctx cancel, goroutines accumulate. reproducer attached. :grimacing:

trent: ugh. which SDK version and sample? can you paste the minimal repro loop?

maya: go-sdk v0.12.7, sample app in /examples/generator. Reduced loop below:

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
iter, err := client.Generator(ctx, model, prompt) // returns StreamIterator
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
// sample didn't call iter.Close() originally
for iter.Next() {
  b := iter.Value()
  process(b)
}
if err := iter.Err(); err != nil {
  log.Printf("generator err: %v", err)
}
```

maya: with concurrent clients + token rotation, logs show `context deadline exceeded` but iter.Next() still blocks; leak detector flagged 5 goroutines.

qiao: that smells like the internal read goroutine is stuck in a socket retry and isn't selecting on ctx.Done() or a close channel. we've had this pattern before.

trent: is there a Close() on the iterator? samples should `defer iter.Close()` after creation. docs might be ambiguous.

maya: sample left it out. adding `defer iter.Close()` fixes the hang in my local repro. but callers will reasonably expect Next to return when the passed ctx cancels. our README text is vague: "Next returns false on EOF or error; check Err()" — doesn't clarify Close vs ctx ownership.

eng-runtime-bot: nightly: stream-leak-checker reported 4 leaked goroutines in generator sample (2026-03-22).

qiao: API options:
1) low effort: update samples + README to always `defer iter.Close()` and add a test asserting Next returns quickly after Close.
2) medium: make Close() safe & idempotent concurrently; ensure internal reader selects on ctx.Done() and closeCh so Next unblocks promptly on either. return a documented error from Err() (e.g., ErrIteratorClosed) if Close caused stop.
3) high: breaking API change to support `NextContext(ctx)` or `NextWithContext(ctx)` so each iteration can be cancelled explicitly. also consider helper `GeneratorWithCancel(ctx)` that returns (iter, cancel).

trent: I like 1+2 for immediate mitigation. for 2 we should be explicit about error semantics: if user closes iterator, Err() should return ErrIteratorClosed; if the user's ctx canceled, Err() should return context.Canceled. we should document errors.Is behavior so consumers can detect both.

maya: tests: I'll add an integration test that spins up 10 goroutines, starts Iterator, forces token rotation, call iter.Close() and assert Next returns within 50ms and Err() matches ErrIteratorClosed.

qiao: runtime note: when the runtime retries connections it may block inside net.Read until timeout; making reads interruptible requires setting deadlines on net.Conn or using context-aware reads. runtime owners pinged: @eng-runtime, please advise.

trent: okay plan: maya will open a docs+sample PR to `defer iter.Close()` and add a repro test. qiao will open SDK PR to make Close idempotent and add fast-unblock path. we'll track NextWithContext in a design ticket.

maya: opening WIP PR now, will link it. thanks y'all. :thumbsup:

eng-runtime-bot: CI reminder: run `make sample-test` and `go test ./... -race` locally before pushing. CI will run stream-leak-checker automatically. :robot_face:
